messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager triggered: CACHE_MISS_CONVOY_LVL2 — high prefix miss rate detected for the text-generation tier. Affected: hosted-prod-us-west. Please acknowledge.

maria.ops: acked. oncall = jordan.oncall. I'm joining. Any customer-impact notes yet?

jordan.oncall: joining now. saw alerts ~5m ago. latency SLOs spiking on /v1/generate and some 503s. Customers reporting slow responses.

kevin.eng: quick data point: prefix hit rate for model-x/seq512 dropped from ~86% to 12% at 17:03 UTC. We see a corresponding jump in GPU qps and token cost.

ravi.sre: linking rapid charts: https://logs.internal/redwood/cache/hitrate?range=30m&series=model-x,model-y (paste: filter=prefix)

maya.prod: customer note: two enterprise orgs reported timeout errors, support ticket ids #63412 and #63419. Marking P1 for those customers.

maria.ops: infra-bot, can you surface recent deploys that touched cache config or versions around 16:50-17:10 UTC?

infra-bot: Recent deploys:
- 16:42 UTC - kevin.eng - feature/kv-prefix-refactor (staging -> canary)
- 16:55 UTC - ops/kv-policy-tweak (flag disable-ttl-sync) (canary -> prod)
- 16:59 UTC - infra/regen-index (prod)

kevin.eng: that 16:42 branch changed how prefix normalization works for some legacy routes. It should have been behind a flag, but canary rollout progressed earlier than expected.

jordan.oncall: hypothesis A: prefix normalization change caused key divergence -> cache cold miss storm. Hypothesis B: ttl-sync flag caused unexpected rapid evictions.

ravi.sre: adding to timeline:
- 16:42 deploy (prefix normalization changed)
- 16:55 ttl-sync disable flag rollout
- 16:59 index regen job kicked off
- 17:03 first miss-rate spike alerts
- 17:07 errors reported by prod clients

maria.ops: collecting logs. kevin, can you paste the relevant diff or config lines?

kevin.eng: share snippet below (diff):
```
- key = f"{model}:{prefix}:{user_id}"
+ key = f"{model}:{normalize_prefix(prefix)}:{user_id}"
```
Normalization strips trailing whitespace and lowercases, but some downstream callers rely on exact-case prefixes (legacy integrations).

nora-support: note — legacy customers use case-sensitive prefixes, we have two open integrations that are case-sensitive. That aligns with affected customer list.

maya.prod: cross-checking supported-model mapping: those integrations call model-x with mixed-case prefixes.

ravi.sre: we pulled logs for a sample key before and after deploy. Example:
```
17:02:59 GET cache key=Model-X:UserABC:prefX -> MISS
17:03:01 GET cache key=model-x:userabc:prefx -> MISS (new normalized form)
17:03:02 backend spawn -> regen
```

jordan.oncall: mitigation plan — short term: rollback normalization or add compatibility layer that normalizes both keys. Which is fastest?

kevin.eng: fastest is to toggle the canary rollout back to previous code path (revert rollout). I can push a rollback to prod canary within 10m. Alternative: hotfix that writes both key forms for a brief period, but that requires more careful testing.

maria.ops: proceed with rollback to minimize customer impact. kevin, you and jordan coordinate. I'll update stakeholders.

kevin.eng: initiating rollback now. command: `deploy rollback canary ops/kv-prefix-refactor --to=prod@16:40`

infra-bot: Rollback job started (job id: rb-2029-17-03). Estimated 8m to full effect across canaries.

ravi.sre: started capturing hit-rate delta and error surface. attaching sample metrics (paste):
- 17:03:00 hit-rate model-x: 12%
- 17:10:00 hit-rate model-x: 35%
- 17:16:00 hit-rate model-x: 74%
- 17:22:00 hit-rate model-x: 85%
- 17:25:00 503/error rate back to baseline

maria.ops: support, please ack ticket owners that we're rolling back and expecting recovery in ~20m.

nora-support: msg sent to customers, included temporary mitigation (use legacy prefix exact-case) and ETA. Customers acknowledged.

jordan.oncall: rollback completed across canaries at 17:11, across prod at 17:18 per deploy logs.

kevin.eng: confirming: we never disabled TTL sync; that flag rollout was separate. Index regen job at 16:59 increased background I/O but not primary cause. Root cause summary so far: canary progressed with prefix normalization change that created divergent keys for legacy integrations -> widespread cache misses -> downstream latency and 503s.

ravi.sre: next steps for RCA:
1) build a concise timeline (we have events)
2) run logshare with key samples and fetch hit/miss traces per customer (I can generate a link)
3) propose follow-ups: revert canary gating model, add integration tests for prefix behaviour, and add an automated canary stop if hit-rate drops >20% within 10m.

maria.ops: +1. Also add a short postmortem action: create a canary healthcheck that includes cache hit-rate for critical routes.

kevin.eng: I'll prepare a patch to add dual-writing for 48h as an optional hotfix if we ever need faster compatibility without full rollback. Will open PR with tests.

maya.prod: collecting customer impact summary for postmortem: two P1 tickets, estimated total affected requests ~45k over 25 minutes, revenue-impact flagged.

jordan.oncall: I'll own the initial incident timeline doc and assign follow-ups. tagging: @kevin.eng (fix), @ravi.sre (metrics), @maria.ops (communication), @nora-support (customer comms).

maria.ops: thanks team. I'll close the pager once we confirm stable for 30m.

ravi.sre: post-rollback monitoring: hit-rate holding at ~86% for 40m and error rates normalized. Marking incident as mitigated.

incident-bot: Incident CACHE_MISS_CONVOY_LVL2 resolved (duration 00:48:21). Summary link: https://incidents.redwood/1749999999

maria.ops: we'll schedule RCA write-up in the incidents backlog, include the timeline, logshare links, diffs, and follow-ups. Closing thread for live coordination.

kevin.eng: PR queued: dual-write shim + unit tests. Will sync in RFC.

nora-support: closing customer comm loop once postmortem is published.

jordan.oncall: handing back to normal ops. If anything flares, ping this thread. :white_check_mark:
